tolerance: Levels: absolute 1e-6 dB. A level is logarithmic, so an absolute bound on dB is a relative bound (2.3e-7) on energy and holds at every scale; the model is closed-form arithmetic with no discretisation, so only floating-point error (<1e-9 dB between the two reference forms) is expected and 1e-6 dB leaves margin for display-independent round-off while being five orders below the 0.1 dB at which thresholds are compared. Energy shares: absolute 1e-6 (dimensionless fraction). EA and durations: relative 1e-6 / 1e-9. Categorical threshold, flag and refusal outcomes: exact. Random cases whose LEX lies within 0.05 dB of a threshold carry no threshold check, so display rounding cannot decide them.

Weekly exposure, octave-band method, CSV import (post-MVP).
EN 458 over-protection (L108 para 83: aim for 70-80 dB(A) at ear) - not a claimed tool feature.
Upper bounds on level (150 dB) and T0 (24 h): tool heuristics without a published basis.
Exports (PDF/CSV/JSON/Python), record import, locale formatting, timeline/chart rendering: not numerical claims answerable by an external reference.
The spec's 100-random-case QA target: the corpus carries 24 random shifts to stay within the 25-80 case budget of the benchmark brief.
coverage: Covers: energy (not dB) summation and LEX over T0; acceptance criteria 'single task reproduces its level' and 'order does not change the total'; spec QA tests single task, equal levels, short high-noise burst, zero-duration rejection; per-task energy contribution and dominant task; total duration; EU 80/85/87 preset with source/jurisdiction and both sides plus equality of every threshold; Art. 3(2) split (action vs ambient, limit vs at-ear); protected estimate via user attenuation, SNR(LC), simplified SNR(LA) with limitation flag, HML both branches, derating, part-time wear; ambient invariance under a protector; user override pack; uncertainty review; invalid/insufficient inputs; 24 randomized shifts.
